note: Each value is the change during that calendar month (a total return, inflation, or AUD/USD move) times scale. null = no data. Month m is at index (m - start) in values.

au_shares.label: Australian shares (total return)

segments.source: Kenneth French Data Library: Australia market portfolio, local currency, dividends included (MSCI data before 2007)
VAS (Vanguard Australian Shares ETF) adjusted close, Yahoo

au_shares.gap: No free monthly total-return data before 1975.

segments.source: Shiller: S&P Composite, monthly average prices + dividends
Kenneth French Data Library: all US stocks (CRSP), dividends included
VTI (Vanguard Morningstar Total Stock Market ETF, called Vanguard Total Stock Market ETF before 29 Jul 2026) adjusted close, Yahoo
STAND-IN: US shares only (no free world data this early)
Rough mix: 50% US shares + 50% French all-country ex-US index
Kenneth French Data Library: developed markets, US$
VGS adjusted close, converted to US$

us_tech.label: US tech-heavy shares (Nasdaq)

segments.source: Nasdaq Composite price index + assumed 0.7% a year dividends
Nasdaq-100 price index + assumed 0.7% a year dividends

us_tech.gap: Price index only; dividends are an assumption (QQQ yields about 0.5-0.7% a year).

au_bonds.label: Australian government bonds

segments.source: Calculated from RBA government bond yields: 85% 5-year + 15% 10-year (10-year only before 1972). End-of-month yields: the RBA's last-business-day figures before 1995, the last daily value from 1995.

au_bonds.gap: Government bonds only; VAF also holds semi-government and corporate bonds, which pay a bit more. The RBA has no 5-year yield for the end of 2013-05, 2013-06, 2013-07, 2013-08 (no figures 20 May to 23 Sep 2013): those 5-year yields are estimated as the 10-year yield plus the 5-year/10-year gap, drawn in a straight line between the months either side, so the returns for 2013-05, 2013-06, 2013-07, 2013-08, 2013-09 are partly estimated.

segments.source: Calculated from Shiller's long-term interest rate (monthly average)
Calculated from FRED GS10 (monthly average)
Calculated from FRED DGS10, end of month

intl_shares.label: Shares outside the US (total return)

segments.source: Kenneth French Data Library: international 'all countries' index (the markets outside the US in its data), US$, dividends included
VEU (Vanguard All-World ex-US Shares ETF) adjusted close, converted to US$, Yahoo

intl_shares.gap: No free data before 1975. Mostly developed markets; emerging markets are only partly covered, so it is a stand-in for VEU's all-world-ex-US index.

gold.label: Gold (US$ price)

segments.source: World Bank Commodity Price Data (Pink Sheet): gold, US$ per troy ounce, average of each month's daily prices (London afternoon fixing; spot from June 2025)
GOLD (Global X Physical Gold) adjusted close, converted to US$, Yahoo

gold.gap: Starts April 1968, when the free market price began (gold was held at about US$35 before). The World Bank figures are monthly averages, which smooth the month-to-month moves a little (true month-end prices swing more), and are whole dollars, so months before about 1973 (gold under US$100) are rounded by up to 1-2%. No income: gold pays nothing.

segments.source: RBA: bank bills to 1976, interbank cash rate to 1990, cash rate target after (monthly average / 12)
Kenneth French Data Library (Ibbotson, then ICE BofA)

au_cpi.label: Australian inflation (CPI)

segments.source: ABS quarterly CPI: each quarter's index (the average of its 3 months) placed at its middle month, with the months in between growing evenly
ABS complete Monthly CPI (the first month is measured from the quarterly chain's level for the month before)

au_cpi.gap: No CPI before 1948 in the ABS series.

us_cpi.label: US inflation (CPI-U)

segments.source: Shiller (Warren-Pearson price index)
BLS CPI-U via FRED

us_cpi.gap: Missing months filled by spreading the change evenly: 2025-10 (no CPI was published, e.g. the Oct 2025 US government shutdown).

audusd.label: AUD/USD (change in US$ per A$1)

segments.source: RBA tables F11, end of month

audusd.gap: Starts July 1969. The A$ was pegged to the British pound until December 1971, then to the US$ until September 1974, then to a basket of currencies until it was floated in December 1983, so most months before the float barely move.

VGS.label: Vanguard MSCI International Shares Index ETF

VDHG.label: Vanguard Diversified High Growth Index ETF

VAF.label: Vanguard Australian Fixed Interest Index ETF

VTI.label: Vanguard Morningstar Total Stock Market ETF

IWLD.label: iShares Core MSCI World ex Australia ESG ETF
IWLD.warning: Tracks developed markets outside Australia with ESG screens (some companies left out); developed-world shares overall stand in for it.

WXOZ.label: State Street SPDR S&P World ex Australia Carbon Aware ETF
WXOZ.warning: Tracks developed markets outside Australia with a carbon tilt (less in heavy emitters); developed-world shares overall stand in for it.

VEU.label: Vanguard All-World ex-US Shares Index ETF
VEU.warning: Before 2013 uses shares outside the US from Kenneth French's data, which are mostly developed markets (VEU also holds emerging markets). No data before 1975.

VTS.label: Vanguard Morningstar US Total Market Shares Index ETF

ETHI.label: Betashares Global Sustainability Leaders ETF
ETHI.warning: A concentrated ethical fund (about 200 large companies, more technology and no fossil fuels); developed-world shares overall are only a rough stand-in.

VESG.label: Vanguard Ethically Conscious International Shares Index ETF
VESG.warning: Ethical screens leave out some industries (e.g. fossil fuels, weapons); developed-world shares overall stand in for it.

QUAL.label: VanEck MSCI International Quality ETF
QUAL.warning: Holds only 'quality' companies (high profits, low debt), so it can do better or worse than the whole developed market for years at a time; developed-world shares overall stand in for it.

MOAT.label: VanEck Morningstar Wide Moat ETF
MOAT.warning: A concentrated fund of about 40-50 US companies chosen by Morningstar; the whole US market stands in for it, so its real returns can differ a lot in any year.

VHY.label: Vanguard Australian Shares High Yield ETF
VHY.warning: No high-dividend share series exists, so Australian shares overall stand in. VHY holds about 70 higher-yielding companies (more banks and miners), so its returns can differ a lot from the whole market in any year.

VAP.label: Vanguard Australian Property Securities Index ETF
VAP.warning: No Australian listed property series exists, so Australian shares overall stand in. Listed property is bumpier than the whole market (it fell roughly three-quarters in 2007-09, versus about half for all shares), so proxy months understate its risk.

VGAD.label: Vanguard MSCI Index International Shares (Hedged) ETF

HGBL.label: Betashares Global Shares Currency Hedged ETF

VDGR.label: Vanguard Diversified Growth Index ETF
VDGR.warning: International bonds (21%, hedged) are approximated by US 10-year Treasuries (hedged). Small companies and emerging markets use developed-world shares as a stand-in.

VDBA.label: Vanguard Diversified Balanced Index ETF
VDBA.warning: International bonds (35%, hedged) are approximated by US 10-year Treasuries (hedged), which swing more with interest rates than VBND's mix of shorter government and company bonds. Small companies and emerging markets use developed-world shares as a stand-in.

VDCO.label: Vanguard Diversified Conservative Index ETF
VDCO.warning: International bonds (42%, hedged) are approximated by US 10-year Treasuries (hedged), which swing more with interest rates than VBND's mix of shorter government and company bonds. Small companies and emerging markets use developed-world shares as a stand-in.

VBND.label: Vanguard Global Aggregate Bond Index (Hedged) ETF
VBND.warning: No free long-run global bond series exists, so US 10-year Treasuries (hedged to A$) stand in. VBND's bonds are shorter (about 6 years' duration, versus about 8 for a 10-year Treasury) and include company and non-US government bonds, so the proxy swings more with interest rates.

GOLD.label: Global X Physical Gold Structured
GOLD.warning: Before 2008 (when its Yahoo prices start) uses the World Bank's monthly average gold price, converted to A$. Averages smooth the moves (about 10% less bumpy month to month than GOLD's real month-end prices) and only loosely match them month by month, though the long-run growth matched well (2008-2026: 9.3% a year real, 9.8% proxy).
